content:
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
Machine Learning Engineer | Data Scientist

Edinburgh, UK | tobias.mwangihartley@example.com | +44 7700 900110 | linkedin.com/in/tmh-example

PROFILE
Data scientist with 6 years in analytics and data science, including 4+ years as a data scientist, building and applying machine learning models for forecasting, customer analytics and retention. Experienced in developing Python models and analytics workflows used by operations and growth teams, with production data workflows using BigQuery, dbt and Vertex AI Workbench. Strong statistical foundation and practical experience translating business questions into measurable analyses and decisions. Moving towards machine learning engineering.

EXPERIENCE

Data Scientist | Thistlebox (meal-kit subscriptions), Edinburgh | Feb 2022–Present
- Built a weekly demand forecasting model for orders per recipe and region, forecasting up to six weeks ahead using LightGBM and calendar, price and menu-position features. WAPE decreased from 23% to 14%, with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste.
- Implemented the forecasting workflow as a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook job, writing forecasts to BigQuery for operations to use in Looker.
- Developed an XGBoost churn propensity model, scored weekly in BigQuery, to target retention offers to top-decile customers. A 10% holdout validation found churn decreased by 2.1 percentage points in the treated group.
- Design and analyse approximately 40 A/B tests per year for growth and product teams; built a Python and Streamlit sequential testing calculator with sequential boundaries, used by around 25 colleagues.
- Wrote the calculator app and Dockerfile; the data platform team handles deployment, with the app hosted on Cloud Run.
- Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer.
- Present results to leadership monthly.

Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail, Glasgow | Sep 2020–Jan 2022
- Conducted customer segmentation and tariff analysis using R and SQL.
- Automated monthly regulator reports using R Markdown.

SELECTED MACHINE LEARNING PROJECT
Image Classification Course Project | Personal | 2025
- Fine-tuned a small CNN in PyTorch on a public food-images dataset as part of an online deep-learning course; achieved approximately 80% accuracy. Learning project.
- Tools: PyTorch, torchvision, Google Colab.

EDUCATION
MSc Statistics | University of the Lothians | 2020 | Distinction
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models for small-area energy demand

BSc Mathematics | University of the Lothians | 2019

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and data: Python (pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, statsmodels), R (tidyverse, brms), SQL (BigQuery)
Machine learning and statistics: Feature engineering, time-series forecasting, churn modelling, A/B testing, causal inference, Bayesian statistics
Tools and platforms: dbt, Vertex AI Workbench, Looker, Streamlit, Docker, Git, Jupyter, PyTorch, torchvision

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Swahili (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, professional, well-structured CV with strong quantified outcomes: WAPE reduced from 23% to 14%, estimated food waste reduced by 9%, and churn reduced by 2.1 percentage points in the treated group. The experience bullets demonstrate practical machine learning, experimentation, business impact and stakeholder communication. The document is also appropriately transparent about the candidate moving toward machine learning engineering and about deployment being handled by the data platform team. The main content limitation is not writing quality but the relatively limited evidence of production software engineering and customer-support AI experience required by this particular role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, simple text formatting, chronological experience, readable date ranges and searchable technology names. It should parse reliably in most ATS platforms. Keyword coverage is good for Python, SQL, BigQuery, dbt, Vertex AI Workbench, Docker, feature engineering, forecasting and machine learning. However, the document does not explicitly use the ATS-friendly term “Google Cloud Platform (GCP)” even though the candidate's tools demonstrate GCP experience. It also lacks evidence or keywords for RAG, chat assistants, model monitoring, data versioning and MLOps tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow or Airflow. For this specific vacancy, the likely AI-screening probability is moderate to low because several mandatory role-specific terms are absent, despite strong matching evidence in forecasting and applied machine learning.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest matches are strong Python, practical machine learning, feature engineering, cloud-based workflows, scheduled processing, BigQuery/dbt data work and measurable business outcomes. The forecasting workflow is particularly relevant evidence of taking a model into operational use, and the Streamlit/Docker/Cloud Run example provides some production software exposure. The candidate's MSc Statistics and BSc Mathematics are relevant quantitative degrees, but the advertised degree requirement specifically asks for machine learning, computer science or a related engineering field. The candidate material does not show at least four years as a machine learning engineer, chat-assistant or RAG experience, or production model monitoring and data versioning. It also does not establish experience preparing large text datasets or integrating language models into products. The role's customer-support AI focus is therefore a substantial domain mismatch, although the CV presents a credible adjacent data-science-to-ML-engineering profile. Culture alignment is not directly evidenced, but the CV does show ownership of analytical tools, practical decision-making and regular communication with leadership.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, ATS-FOCUSED IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Technical Skills section under “Tools and platforms,” explicitly add the supported cloud-provider name: change “dbt, Vertex AI Workbench, Looker, Streamlit, Docker, Git, Jupyter, PyTorch, torchvision” to “Google Cloud Platform (GCP): BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Cloud Run; dbt, Looker, Streamlit, Docker, Git, Jupyter, PyTorch, torchvision.” This makes the existing GCP experience easier for ATS screening to identify without adding an unsupported technology.
2. In the Data Scientist | Thistlebox experience section, revise the forecasting workflow bullet to make its operational pipeline context more explicit while remaining accurate: change “Implemented the forecasting workflow as a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook job, writing forecasts to BigQuery for operations to use in Looker” to “Implemented a scheduled Google Cloud forecasting workflow in Vertex AI Workbench, writing model outputs to BigQuery for operational use in Looker.”
3. In the same Thistlebox section, make the supported feature-engineering evidence more searchable by revising the forecasting bullet to include the exact phrase “feature engineering”: change “using LightGBM and calendar, price and menu-position features” to “using LightGBM with feature engineering for calendar, price and menu-position features.”
4. In the Profile section, avoid presenting the headline as if the candidate already has the advertised job title. Change “Machine Learning Engineer | Data Scientist” to “Data Scientist | Applied Machine Learning” and retain “Moving towards machine learning engineering” in the profile. This keeps the positioning ambitious but fully consistent with the documented employment history.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "Machine Learning Engineer" (as a current professional title)
unsupported_claims: "Machine Learning Engineer" (as a current professional title)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable and professionally written. It presents strong quantified outcomes, including a reduction in forecast WAPE from 23% to 14%, an estimated 9% reduction in food waste, and a 2.1 percentage-point reduction in churn. The experience is credible and appropriately distinguishes the candidate's own work from work handled by the data platform team. The main content limitation is not writing quality but role fit: the CV presents a strong data scientist profile while the target role requires a production-oriented machine learning engineer with customer-support AI experience. The profile statement "Moving towards machine learning engineering" is honest, but also signals that the candidate may not yet meet the seniority implied by the vacancy.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, plain text formatting, conventional dates and clear employer/job-title structure. Relevant terms such as Python, feature engineering, forecasting, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Cloud Run, Docker, dbt and production SQL are present. However, automated screening may score it lower because it does not contain supported evidence for several high-priority terms in the advertisement, including model serving, monitoring, data versioning, AI assistants, RAG, language models, CI/CD, automated testing, MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow and text-data processing. These are candidate experience gaps rather than terms that should be added without evidence. The CV could nevertheless improve keyword precision by describing the supported scheduled notebook workflow, Cloud Run boundary, model scoring process and Docker work more explicitly. Estimated AI-screening probability: moderate-to-low for this specific Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI vacancy, despite strong parsing compatibility.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with Python, GCP, feature engineering, statistical modelling, forecasting, customer analytics, scheduled production workflows and business-facing ML applications. The candidate demonstrates practical ML delivery through LightGBM and XGBoost models, BigQuery scoring, Vertex AI Workbench, Looker, dbt and Cloud Run. The degree in Statistics and Mathematics is closely quantitative but is not explicitly a degree in machine learning, computer science or an engineering field. The candidate's material does not establish at least four years specifically as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production. It also does not show AI products such as chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation, production monitoring, data versioning, language-model fine-tuning, model serving ownership, or data-ingestion pipelines. The scheduled Vertex AI Workbench workflow provides some relevant orchestration evidence, but the CV does not demonstrate the named MLOps tools in the advert. There is good evidence of ownership, pragmatism and communicating context through independently built analytical tools and regular leadership presentations, but the CV does not directly evidence teamwork with backend engineers or support-operations AI.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Profile section, replace the final sentence "Moving towards machine learning engineering" with a more role-relevant but equally truthful summary of current evidence, such as: "Experienced in developing and operationalising Python machine-learning workflows on GCP, including scheduled forecasting and weekly customer-scoring processes, and now targeting production machine-learning engineering roles." Do not describe the candidate as a machine learning engineer or claim ownership of production infrastructure.

2. In the Data Scientist section under Thistlebox, revise the Vertex AI bullet to make the supported orchestration and data-flow evidence more explicit: "Implemented a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook job for weekly forecasting, writing model outputs to BigQuery for operational use in Looker." This uses the portfolio's exact evidence and makes the workflow easier for ATS and recruiters to identify.

3. In the same Thistlebox section, revise the Cloud Run bullet to preserve the important ownership boundary while exposing relevant software-engineering keywords: "Built the Streamlit sequential-testing calculator and Dockerfile; the data platform team handled deployment and hosted the containerised app on Cloud Run." Do not change this to "deployed" or "owned production serving," because the original material says deployment was handled by the data platform team.

4. In the Technical Skills section, add the supported technologies currently present in the CV body but not grouped as clearly as possible: include "Cloud Run" and "Vertex AI Workbench" under cloud/platforms, and include "Docker" and "Streamlit" under tools. Also add "scheduled notebook jobs" or "scheduled ML workflows" only if phrased as a workflow capability rather than as an unsupported MLOps tool.

5. In the Technical Skills section, add "SHAP" under the machine-learning or model-interpretability skills because it is documented in the candidate portfolio for the churn project. Do not add MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow, RAG, chat assistants, monitoring, data versioning, CI/CD, or model serving unless the candidate can substantiate those experiences; they are not present in the supplied original information.

6. In the Experience section under Thistlebox, consider adding the supported regional and feature detail to the forecasting bullet: "Built a weekly LightGBM demand-forecasting model for orders per recipe and region, forecasting six weeks ahead using calendar, price and menu-position features." This more directly matches the advertisement's feature-engineering and forecasting terminology without overstating the system's scope.
